name: Aflibercept
route_note: intravitreal injection every 4–16 weeks for eye disease; IV infusion every two weeks (ziv-aflibercept) for colorectal cancer
owner: Regeneron (US, Eylea); Bayer (outside US); Sanofi (Zaltrap); biosimilars

discovery.by: Jocelyn Holash, George Yancopoulos and colleagues, Regeneron
discovery.note: A decoy receptor fusing VEGFR1 domain 2 and VEGFR2 domain 3 to human IgG1 Fc, binding VEGF with very high affinity.

tagline: VEGF trap fusion protein used for retinal disease and metastatic colorectal cancer
summary: Aflibercept is a recombinant fusion protein that acts as a soluble decoy receptor for VEGF-A, VEGF-B and placental growth factor. As Eylea it treats wet macular degeneration, diabetic macular oedema and retinal vein occlusion with less frequent injections than earlier agents; as ziv-aflibercept (Zaltrap) it is used with chemotherapy in metastatic colorectal cancer.
mechanism: Aflibercept combines the binding domains of VEGFR1 and VEGFR2, so it traps VEGF-A, VEGF-B and placental growth factor before they reach their receptors, with higher affinity than the native receptors.

In the eye this suppresses choroidal neovascularisation and vascular leakage; in tumours it limits angiogenesis needed for growth. The long intraocular activity permits dosing every eight weeks or longer after loading doses.
uses: Diabetic macular oedema and diabetic retinopathy
Macular oedema after retinal vein occlusion

history.title: VEGF Trap
history.detail: Regeneron describes the VEGF-Trap decoy receptor in PNAS.

history.title: Eye approval
history.detail: FDA approves Eylea for wet AMD based on the VIEW 1 and VIEW 2 trials.

history.title: Cancer approval
history.detail: Ziv-aflibercept (Zaltrap), with Sanofi, approved for metastatic colorectal cancer; EU approves Eylea.

history.title: Diabetic macular oedema
history.detail: FDA approves Eylea for diabetic macular oedema.

history.title: Eylea HD
history.detail: An 8 mg high-dose formulation allowing intervals up to 16 weeks is approved.

history.title: Biosimilars
history.detail: FDA approves the first aflibercept biosimilars, including interchangeable products; launches are delayed by patent litigation.

pk.half_life: about 5–6 days systemic after IV; free drug undetectable soon after intravitreal dosing
pk.bioavailability: low systemic exposure after intravitreal use

serious: haemorrhage, gastrointestinal perforation and impaired wound healing (IV)
